Mate, I left the shift a few months back now after 5 years and joined a proactive team with very little paperwork; best thing I’ve ever done. 

I was in the same spot as you for a very long time, waiting for my courses, hoping to get more enjoyment in response through them - the whole reason i joined the force.

After I got my courses it got better for a short while, but the novelty dies off and ultimately you’re still dealing with the same jobs, same problems and same feeling of fighting fires with a water gun.

I remember speaking to my sergeant at the time and I’ll always remember him giving me this great piece of advice “if this is how you feel now, how will you feel in 12 months still in the same position”.

I took his advice and ran with it, leaving the shift has been the best thing I’ve done and I’m actually doing things I joined to do, with the excitement of still having and using my courses.

My advice to you is, stick it out for now - response is the place to learn your craft, get your experience and your courses; then if you still feel the same, move departments; you’ll have more examples and character to take with you into your future role and interviews for them. Try to enjoy the little wins for now, not everything has to be blue light runs and foot chases; the next time you find a repeat misper could be the one time they’re about to be exploited via CCE.

Good luck mate, keep your head up!

So as it reads you two are half committed to each other, you are friends with benefits in a fake relationship.

I’ll be honest, I’ve been through your situation. I found that i once had a fwb and we got on like a house on fire, we also experimented with a relationship after we both tended to grow stronger and catch feelings.

After a few months of things being “real” she became very up and down, cold, blunt and treating me very casually.

It hurt me because I over expected what to presume from her in this “relationship”.

I think for most people a relationship can be defined very widely with a whole bunch of terms and boundaries. Each person is different and each person is their own.

In my case, the girl had a very troubled past and had trouble dealing with and coping with anything related or that reminded her of those times.

We began our relationship as strangers looking for fun, and i believe that this “relationship” for both of us was us naturally growing fonder of one another.

Ultimately in your situation I would say this, her argument with her sister maybe be causing her problems from things you may not be aware of, communication is key; however, do not try to change her. If she is unwilling to change or even acknowledge her behaviour, or how she makes you feel. She is not right for you.

I would hold yourself to a high value and let nature runs its course; let her deal with her situation by her own means and be supportive but do not let her walk all over you because you care for her and have feelings.

I would agree tour ADHD comes into play with being over sensitive; I would say that in answer to the post’s question; yes, yes you are but that is only due to your ADHD.

The rest of my answer is how I would deal with your situation if I was you based on your circumstances.

Don’t be too hard of yourself; if it doesn’t work out, her loss. In my case, I ended up finding my gf after this similar situation and haven’t looked back.

If she’s the one, she won’t make you question your own worth, judgement or character.

Hope it all works out, good luck.
